background.objective: The objective of this pilot is to prove the value of Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience (GECX) against Afni-prioritized workflows. Premier Cloud and Afni will collaborate to design and build voice agents exercised against representative Afni scenarios and data samples, and measured on Afni-relevant criteria such as call containment and deflection, intent-resolution accuracy, average handle time versus Afni's 44-minute baseline, and tool-call accuracy. The pilot produces a tangible reference point that lets Afni's intelligent-automation team evaluate GECX, its native voice channel on the Google Telephony Platform (GTP), and Google Cloud's open agent platform on Afni-specific evidence.
business_challenges: Level 1 interactions are high-volume, repeatable, and knowledge-article-driven — L1 resolves up to ~80% of reported issues by following existing knowledge articles — and the team is exploring whether a voice-agent capability could measurably extend service delivery without proportional headcount expansion.

The team is interested in expanding multi-channel customer-facing agent deployment — voice, chat, and website-embedded — and is evaluating capability that fits this without the per-channel licensing constraints observed with current tooling.

Agent experimentation runs in parallel across UiPath, Copilot Studio, custom Python, and emerging open frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph), and the team is looking for a unified governance and observability plane across these multi-platform efforts.

Afni's broader push to embed AI into more roles benefits from concrete, observable evidence on a near-term timeline to inform investment direction and to demonstrate progress to executive stakeholders.

scope.statement: Afni's high-volume, script-driven contact workflows — across both its internal IT Service Desk and its insurance subrogation operations — are strong candidates for AI-augmented voice, where a GECX agent can measurably extend service delivery and recovery capacity.
out_of_scope_extra: The Workspace License sales motion currently in progress with Afni's identity-management group is a separate Premier Cloud engagement and not part of this SOW.
A full Azure-to-Google-Cloud infrastructure migration is out of scope for this pilot and will be addressed under separate Premier Cloud engagements.
Configuration, deployment, or licensing of the Wiz security platform is out of scope.
The Progressive CCC follow-up / status-chase cycle and the broader insurance FNOL intake workflow beyond adverse-carrier identification are out of scope for this pilot.

Production outbound-dialing infrastructure and telephony compliance for the insurance agents at scale are out of scope for the pilot; the pilot exercises representative outbound calls through the Google Telephony Platform, with the production approach delivered as a recommendation.
Building or deploying a centralized multi-agent governance dashboard for Afni's UiPath, Copilot Studio, and custom-agent estates is a potential future phase and not included in this pilot.
Net-new chatbot deployments outside the pilot's voice-agent scope (e.g., website-embedded support chat) are out of scope.
Development of new machine-learning models within Azure or Azure AI Foundry is out of scope.
Modification, refactoring, or migration of Afni's existing UiPath Robotic Process Automation flows is out of scope.
Modification, refactoring, or migration of Afni's existing Microsoft Copilot Studio agents is out of scope.

use_cases.name: IT Service desk
use_cases.summary: demonstrates end-to-end Level 1 handling — mandatory employee verification on every call, then resolution of the priority use cases (login & MFA assistance, Citrix troubleshooting, VPN & connectivity, and the new-hire technical check) by retrieving the relevant service-desk knowledge article and guiding the caller step by step.
use_cases.current_solution: The current IT Service Desk workflow proceeds as follows:
current_solution_steps: **Initial Contact:** Calls arrive at the Cisco / WebEx Contact Center IVR, which performs basic triage and automatically creates an IMS interaction ticket in ServiceNow.
**Routing:** The call is routed to a live Level 1 (L1) analyst.
**Identity Verification:** The L1 analyst verifies the caller's identity across several systems, including UMS, Angel, ServiceNow, and the Work From Home Helper App.

**Triage and Resolution:** The analyst gathers the user's concern, converts the initial IMS interaction into an official Request or Incident ticket, and attempts resolution using the appropriate knowledge article.
**Escalation:** If the L1 analyst cannot resolve the issue, the call is escalated to Level 2.
use_cases.proposed_solution: Premier Cloud will design, build, and demonstrate an IT Service Desk voice agent powered by Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience, in a controlled pilot environment within Afni's Google Cloud Platform. The pilot will be designed to exercise realistic service-desk workflows while avoiding disruption to live operations. The voice agent will integrate with a representative configuration of Afni's ServiceNow environment and employee-verification sources through OpenAPI-based connectors. The voice agent's guided resolution experience will be grounded in Afni's existing service-desk knowledge articles. During each call, the agent will identify the employee's intent, guide the caller through approved troubleshooting steps, determine whether the issue can be resolved, and create or update a ServiceNow ticket when required. For unresolved or higher-complexity issues, the agent will support a warm transfer to Level 2 support, including relevant context captured during the interaction. Call transcripts will be redacted on the Partner side before being attached to ServiceNow records.
use_cases.trigger: Inbound call via the Google Telephony Platform voice channel

use_cases.name: Insurance Services — Progressive CCC (Outbound Claim Filing)
use_cases.summary: an API-triggered agent that calls the Other Insurance Carrier (OIC) to file subrogation claims, validate claim/policy details, and confirm coverage and liability — writing the outcome and a case note back to Subro Assist, CCT, and ClaimPro.
use_cases.current_solution: Progressive CCC subrogation claim filing is an outbound process run against the CCT, ClaimPro, and Subro Assist systems of record. Today, an analyst first reviews the claim — confirming the ClaimPro contact assignment and fault, and locating the Other Insurance Carrier (OIC) details and the claim adjuster contact — then calls the OIC to file the claim, validating the claim or policy/reference number, confirming active coverage, and assessing liability. Voicemail or hold scenarios remain in the phone-filing cycle. Where an online filing path is available it is attempted first, converting to a phone call when the online filing cannot be completed, and the analyst documents throughout in ClaimPro.
use_cases.proposed_solution: Premier Cloud will build and demonstrate an outbound Progressive CCC voice agent on Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience within a controlled pilot environment in Afni's Google Cloud tenant. Execution is triggered via an API endpoint — callable manually by project administrators or driven by automated processes tracking a work list — enabling dispatch from internal source environments without manual initiation of dialer sequences. Briefed with pre-call data from CCT, ClaimPro, and Subro Assist, the agent dials the OIC, identifies itself as an automated agent working on Afni's behalf, files the claim, validates policy details, and confirms coverage and liability on-script per the documented system prompt and decision tree. Within the pilot scope, effort is concentrated on core claim execution; multi-day status tracking is a candidate for a future phase. The agent writes results, final disposition, and redacted transcript summaries back to the systems of record, publishing case notes to Subro Assist via API. Exceptions and unresolved interactions are routed to a live analyst with full interaction context. Outbound calls are delivered through the Google Telephony Platform as the pilot entry channel; the production dialing strategy and compliance framework are delivered as a recommendation.
use_cases.trigger: API endpoint — manual dispatch by a project administrator, or automated from a work list

use_cases.name: Insurance Services — FNOL (Outbound Adverse-Carrier Identification)
use_cases.summary: a separate agent, triggered from Subro Assist work baskets, that calls across carriers to identify the adverse/third-party carrier and returns the result to the underwriting (UM) team, with the same case-note write-back.
use_cases.current_solution: First Notice of Loss (FNOL) adverse-carrier identification is a separate outbound process that spans multiple carriers. When the subrogation team identifies that insurance exists on a claim, it routes the claim to the FNOL team through work baskets in Subro Assist, provided third-party carrier (TPC) information is present. The FNOL team then calls to identify and confirm the adverse / third-party carrier — multiple calls across clients and carriers may be required — and, once identified, files the information via phone or online and returns it to the underwriting (UM) / insurance team.
use_cases.proposed_solution: Premier Cloud will design, build, and demonstrate a separate outbound FNOL voice agent powered by Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience. It is kept independent from the Progressive CCC agent because it spans multiple carriers and serves a distinct objective — carrier identification rather than claim filing. The agent is triggered from Subro Assist work baskets: it queries the Subro Assist API for the items assigned to the voice agent, then places the outbound call to identify the adverse / third-party carrier. Briefed pre-call from CCT, ClaimPro, and Subro Assist, it conducts the call on-script per the prompt and decision tree, captures and validates the identified carrier information, and returns it to the UM / insurance team. The outcome, status, and a redacted conversation summary are written back as case notes to Subro Assist via API, and exceptions or unresolved cases are handed off to a human analyst with the captured context.
use_cases.trigger: Subro Assist work basket, wired through a queue or Pub/Sub topic

risks.risk: Pilot-environment access delays from Afni IT
risks.mitigation: Phase 1 prerequisite confirmation, named technical contact for pilot-environment provisioning, escalation path via PM and Technical Lead

risks.risk: Backend API integration complexity exceeds initial estimates
risks.mitigation: Phase 2 architecture and design review checkpoint, formal written Change Request process for material scope changes

risks.risk: Decision-tree complexity for the pilot scenarios exceeds the agreed pilot scope
risks.mitigation: Phase 1 scoping session with explicit boundary on conversation flows, intent categories, and entity-extraction coverage

risks.risk: GECX voice (GTP) channel latency variance under representative load
risks.mitigation: Phase 2 latency-target design, Phase 4 latency tuning iterations, observability captured in conversational-insights dashboard

risks.risk: Afni-side resource availability constraining joint UAT participation
risks.mitigation: Weekly PM cadence, early surfacing of resource blockers, flexible UAT scheduling around Afni operational windows

risks.risk: Stakeholder turnover during the pilot impacting continuity of approvals and scope decisions
risks.mitigation: Documented decisions and design approvals, clear RACI, named alternate technical contacts, final pilot review meeting to formalize close-out

risks.risk: Outbound-calling infrastructure for the insurance agents is unresolved (GECX-native outbound vs. a separate telephony path)
risks.mitigation: Phase 1/2 infrastructure research and a design decision with Afni; the pilot exercises representative outbound calls via the Google Telephony Platform, with the production dialing approach and compliance delivered as a recommendation

risks.risk: Subro Assist / CCT / ClaimPro API availability, schema, or access is not confirmed
risks.mitigation: Phase 1 prerequisite for documented endpoints and access; sample-data fallback where needed; written Change Request if integration complexity exceeds estimates

risks.risk: Three agents within a fixed-price, eight-week pilot constrains the depth achievable per agent
risks.mitigation: Per-agent MVP scope bounded in Phase 1 with representative scenarios; complex items deferred to the follow-up roadmap or addressed through a written Change Request

success_criteria: Each of the three agents demonstrates end-to-end handling across the pilot scenarios agreed in Phase 1 — the IT Service Desk agent performing mandatory employee verification and guided Level 1 resolution; the Progressive CCC agent placing an API-triggered outbound call to file a claim and confirm coverage and liability; and the FNOL agent placing an outbound call to identify the adverse / third-party carrier — each writing results back to its system of record (ServiceNow or Subro Assist).
Measurements against the agreed per-agent success metrics are captured and shared with Afni stakeholders.
Afni's intelligent-automation team is trained on agent operation, monitoring, and platform tuning, with documented training materials delivered.
A final pilot report and follow-up roadmap are delivered and reviewed with Afni stakeholders at the pilot close.
